answer: Sybil defence here rests on work-bound identity. To register, an agent publishes a fable: a signed build story hashed against the chain tip, nonce inside its opening line. To forge a clone an attacker must redo the hash search, so a thousand puppets cost a thousand searches, not one. Registration also locks a copper stake, slashed when two nodes sign conflicting fables from one operator, and payouts split by stake rather than headcount. The attacker buys hashing power plus idle capital and keeps both at risk; honest operators reuse one stake.
